Manatee County Administrative Procedures Manual
RLS Electronic Submission Procedure 
Procedure #: 26-104.001 
Purpose 
To facilitate the submission of Requests for Legal Services (RLSs) to the County Attorney’s 
Office (CAO) by providing County team members with clear instructions on submitting all 
information necessary for the CAO to deliver timely, accurate, and effective legal advice.  
Procedure 
To best facilitate the submission of RLSs to the CAO, County team members authorized to 
submit RLSs will do so by the following procedures: 
1. All RLSs must be submitted to the CAO via email to: RLS@mymanatee.org. 
2. The transmittal email submitting an RLS is for delivery purposes only.  Do not include 
any facts, background, summaries, explanations, or substantive information in the body 
of the email.  All relevant information must be included in the RLS Submission Form or in 
properly labeled attachments.  The CAO will not review or rely upon any information 
contained in the email body. 
3. The RLS Submission Form should be completed by the County team member, signed or 
initialed by the Department Director or the appropriate designee when required, and 
attached to the RLS submission email. 
4. Confidential information or documents that cannot be transmitted electronically should 
be sent to the CAO via hand-delivery or interoffice mail. Please indicate the RLS 
subject/title, contact person, extension on the outside of the transmittal envelope. 
Include the RLS Number furnished by the CAO if already provided. 
5. Once a new RLS is accepted by the CAO, it is assigned a sequential RLS Number 
(consisting of the fiscal year designator followed by a number). The submitting 
department will receive two emails: (1) an email acknowledging receipt of the RLS and 
providing its RLS Number; and (2) an email containing the names of the legal team 
assigned to the RLS. 
6. Complete the RLS Submission Form fields as indicated below:

a. Subject/Title: Brief title for the matter to be reviewed. The CAO law office 
management system limits the subject/title to 50 characters. The CAO may rename 
the subject/title consistent with best practices or to accommodate the system’s 
character limitations. 
b. Department/Division: The name of the department or division submitting the 
request. 
c. Account Key: Ten or more-digit number necessary for reporting purposes by the 
CAO and the Financial Management Department. 
d. Contact Person and Extension: The name and phone extension for the County 
team member with the most knowledge regarding the request and who will be 
available to answer questions or provide additional information for the CAO. 
e. Department Director: The name of the director of the department submitting the 
request. 
f. Signature: The Department Director’s signature is required if the request is 
critical or urgent. Critical or urgent requests require the CAO’s immediate attention 
because County team members need a response from the CAO in 15 working days 
or less or the County will suffer some adverse result or consequence. To 
calculate working days, begin counting from the next day (that is not a Saturday, 
Sunday, or County holiday) after the date the RLS is submitted and only count 
days that are not Saturdays, Sundays, or County holidays. 
g. Legal guidance on public records request: This box should only be 
checked/utilized for RLSs submitted by the Public Records Department. If checked, 
the only other section of form which should be completed is “Copies of RLS 
Response to”.  The remainder of the form should be left blank. Public Records 
Department team members should attach the public records request to the RLS 
submission email along with this form. Any documents that need to be reviewed with 
this RLS should be sent to the CAO via hand-delivery or interoffice mail.  
h. Legal question and factual background: Description of the legal issue containing 
relevant facts the assigned legal team will need to understand to fully analyze the 
request. Background or historical information relevant to the request should be 
included. Include information regarding issues that may impact the request. This box 
is limited to 2,000 characters. If more than 2,000 characters are needed to explain 
the legal question and factual background, an additional page of explanation can be 
added to the RLS submission email and should be named “Supplemental Legal 
Question and Factual Background.” 
i. Services requested: Check the box(es) for desired legal services requested from 
the CAO. The CAO will determine if a written response in the form of a memorandum 
is appropriate.

j. Time considerations: 
1) Critical/urgent/not urgent (required): Select either critical/urgent or not urgent. 
Critical or urgent requests require the CAO’s immediate attention because County 
team members need a response from the CAO in 15 working days or less or the 
County will suffer some adverse result or consequence. To calculate working 
days, begin counting from the next day (that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or 
County holiday) after the date the RLS is submitted and only count days that are 
not Saturdays, Sundays, or County holidays. The Department Director’s 
signature is required if the request is critical or urgent. 
2) Date of Board meeting: If applicable, add the date of the planned Board of 
County Commissioners (land use, regular or work session) or Planning 
Commission meeting where the RLS subject matter will be considered. If a 
response is needed for another type of hearing or meeting, the date and hearing 
or meeting type can also be added here, for example: “Hearing Officer on Month 
Day, Year.” 
3) Advertising deadline: If applicable, add the date of the first advertising deadline 
for the ordinance or resolution. 
4) Business Impact Estimate (BIE): If a BIE is required (see Section 125.66(3), 
Florida Statutes), please check this box. The CAO will not be responsible for 
drafting the BIE but can provide a sample BIE upon request or review a draft BIE 
for legal sufficiency. 
5) Date when RLS response is needed (required): Add the date when the CAO’s 
response is needed. This date should take into consideration time for County 
team members to review, address, and otherwise act upon the CAO’s legal 
advice, including any coordination with other parties. Notwithstanding the 
foregoing, the County Attorney reserves the right to establish/determine a 
reasonable response deadline for any RLS, based on the legal demands placed 
on the CAO, the complexity of the request, the volume of materials submitted, 
and any other relevant factors. 
6) Explanation of deadline requested for RLS response (required): An 
explanation of why the RLS response is needed by the date requested. Please 
include any relevant deadlines imposed by others here.

be relevant or related to the RLS.
